title: Countable Mittag-Leffler towers are acyclic for inverse limit
statement: Let $(B_n,g_n:B_{n+1}\to B_n)_{n\geq1}$ be an inverse system of abelian groups [def-weil-inverse-system]. Suppose it is Mittag-Leffler [def-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-system]: for every $n$ the images of $B_m\to B_n$ are constant for all sufficiently large $m$. Then $R^q\varprojlim_n B_n=0$ for every $q\geq1$, where the right derived functors of inverse limit on the abelian category of towers are those of [lem-pc-derived-limit-roos-abelian-groups].

proof.text: Write $t_{m,i}=g_i\circ\cdots\circ g_{m-1}:B_m\to B_i$ for $m\geq i$, with $t_{i,i}=1$. Define towers $P_n=\prod_{1\leq i\leq n}B_i$ and $Q_n=\prod_{1\leq i<n}B_i$, with transition maps forgetting the last coordinate; $Q_1=0$. Define $j_n:B_n\to P_n$ by $j_n(b)_i=t_{n,i}(b)$ and $d_n:P_n\to Q_n$ by $d_n(x)_i=x_i-g_i(x_{i+1})$ for $i<n$. The equality $t_{n+1,i}=t_{n,i}g_n$ shows that $j$ commutes with transitions. Both ways of composing $d$ with a transition have coordinates $x_i-g_i(x_{i+1})$ for $i<n$, so $d$ also commutes with transitions. These are morphisms of towers in the sense of [def-weil-inverse-system].

source.place: Tag 07KW, lemma-compute-Rlim, proof: the finite-prefix systems and their difference map.

proof.text: The sequence $0\to B_n\xrightarrow{j_n}P_n\xrightarrow{d_n}Q_n\to0$ is exact for every $n$. The last coordinate of $j_n(b)$ is $b$, so $j_n$ is injective. A tuple in $\ker d_n$ satisfies $x_i=g_i(x_{i+1})$; descending substitution gives $x_i=t_{n,i}(x_n)$, so it equals $j_n(x_n)$. Conversely these identities give $d_nj_n=0$. Given $y\in Q_n$, set $x_n=0$ and successively set $x_i=y_i+g_i(x_{i+1})$ for $i=n-1,\ldots,1$; then $d_n(x)=y$. At $n=1$ this is $0\to B_1\xrightarrow{1}B_1\to0\to0$. Thus Step 1 gives a short exact sequence of towers.

source.place: Tag 07KW, lemma-compute-Rlim, proof: the finite-prefix systems and their difference map.

proof.text: Apply clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-limit-exact] to $0\to B\xrightarrow{j}P\xrightarrow{d}Q\to0$. The index set is the positive integers, the groups are abelian, Steps 1 and 2 give compatible maps and levelwise exactness, and its kernel tower is precisely the given Mittag-Leffler tower $B$ (not $P$ or $Q$). The cited statement therefore gives a surjection $\varprojlim d:\varprojlim P_n\to\varprojlim Q_n$.

source.place: Tag 02N1, lemma-Mittag-Leffler, clause (3); its proof refers to algebra.tex Tag 0598, lemma-ML-exact-sequence.

proof.text: Identify both limits of Step 3 with $\prod_{i\geq1}B_i$ explicitly. A family $x=(x_i)$ gives the compatible prefixes $(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ in $P_n$ and $(x_1,\ldots,x_{n-1})$ in $Q_n$. Conversely a compatible family of prefixes determines $x_i$ from level $i$ in $P$, and from level $i+1$ in $Q$; projection compatibility makes these values independent of every larger level and recovers all coordinates. These constructions are mutually inverse homomorphisms. Under them, the $i$th coordinate of $\varprojlim d$ is calculated at any level $n>i$ and is $x_i-g_i(x_{i+1})$. Hence Step 3 says that the actual Roos difference map $1-s:\prod_iB_i\to\prod_iB_i$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 07KW, lemma-compute-Rlim, proof: the finite-prefix systems and their difference map.

proof.text: By [lem-pc-derived-limit-roos-abelian-groups], the first right derived inverse limit of this same tower is $\operatorname{coker}(1-s)$. Step 4 makes this cokernel zero: every element of the target product lies in the image, so its quotient by that image is zero. The same cited statement gives $R^q\varprojlim B_n=0$ for every $q\geq2$ without any extra hypothesis. Together with the $q=1$ case this proves the assertion for every positive $q$.
